obligation: Report the fraudulent wire to the custodian and request a recall
citation: Custodial and adviser service agreements (contract); payment system practice
trigger: A money movement the adviser submitted is suspected to be fraudulent
deadline: Immediately on discovery, before anything else; recall chances fall within hours
notify: Custodian adviser fraud line (phone), then in writing; the custodian contacts the receiving bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the most time-critical step. Not a legal notice

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Unauthorized access to electronic personal information of a Florida resident (name plus SSN, ID number, or financial account number with a required access code or password; or a user name or email address with a password)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Delay only on a written law enforcement request (4)(b)
notify: Each affected Florida individual by mail to the address on file, or by email to the address on file (4)(d). In a business email compromise, use mail: the client's email may be controlled by the attacker
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FTC rules set no individual notice, so the federal-regulator deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) does not help. Counsel decides; plan to the 30-day clock

obligation: Florida no-harm determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the adviser reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if relied on. Not expected when a client has already lost money

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: No at current size - customer information covers about 160 consumers; recheck the count in every incident

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No at current size

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the adviser (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains a system for the adviser (CRM, email suite, portfolio platform, e-signature) has a breach of security
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty of the SaaS vendors; the adviser then owes the notices above

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information without the individual's authorization, involving at least 500 consumers. Treated as discovered on the first day known to the adviser or its agents
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, through the online form on ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Applies, but cannot be triggered while customer information covers fewer than 500 consumers (about 160 today). Count affected consumers in every incident

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Affected clients who live outside Florida (five households today)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents, and state regulators where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of every affected client; counsel applies each state's law

obligation: Report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center
trigger: Fraudulent wire from business email compromise
deadline: As soon as possible after discovery; a fast report can help freeze funds
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports the custodian's recall and any law enforcement delay request

obligation: Florida OFR notice of a cyber incident
trigger: Security incident at a Florida-registered adviser
deadline: Not verified
applies_at_this_tier: UNVERIFIED: no incident notice duty for advisers was found in the Chapter 517 sections reviewed, and Rule 69W-600 could not be retrieved. Counsel and the compliance consultant confirm whether any OFR notice or Form ADV update is needed

obligation: Errors and omissions insurance notice
trigger: Loss or claim from fraud or a security incident
deadline: Per policy; notify the carrier before hiring response vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Only if coverage exists - no cyber policy; check the errors and omissions policy for a social engineering or cyber endorsement

obligation: SEC Regulation S-P customer notification
trigger: Unauthorized access to sensitive customer information at a covered institution
deadline: No later than 30 days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: No - covers only advisers registered with the SEC (248.30(d)(3)); becomes the rule if the adviser registers with the SEC

obligation: Suspicious activity report (investment advisers)
citation: 31 CFR Part 1032 (FinCEN investment adviser AML rule; FR Doc. 2025-24184)
trigger: Suspicious transaction conducted through an investment adviser
deadline: Not in effect: effective date delayed to 2028-01-01
applies_at_this_tier: No - covers SEC-registered and exempt reporting advisers only, and is not yet effective. The custodian decides on its own reports

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
applies_at_this_tier: Not in a business email compromise (no ransom); kept for extortion scenarios (POL-01 10.5)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: Banking organization notification incident
trigger: Notification incident at a banking organization
deadline: No later than 36 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a bank or bank holding company

obligation: Credit union reportable cyber incident
trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a credit union

obligation: NYDFS cybersecurity incident and extortion payment
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a NYDFS-regulated entity; extortion payment
deadline: 72 hours after determination; 24 hours after payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - not New York licensed

obligation: Insurance licensee cybersecurity event
citation: NAIC Model #668 sec. 6 (as adopted by states)
trigger: Cybersecurity event at an insurance licensee
deadline: 72 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - no insurance license

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an SEC reporting company

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts
